internal_alignment: Phonemic awareness RF.1.2(a)-(d): distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words; orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds including consonant blends; isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds; segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds. Oral-first: no printed target words for the child, keeping phonemic awareness distinct from printed phonics. Internal record only; no standards codes appear on any child page, and no separate answer key is published for this pack.
pack: Grade 1 Reading: Sounds in Words: Blends and Middle Vowels

pages_detail.activities: Adult-led oral example first (name LONG, map SHORT), then 8 items: picture plus LONG/SHORT pills to circle.
pages_detail.title: Long or Short?

pages_detail.activities: Adult says the sounds one at a time with a short pause; the child blends them and circles the matching picture.
answers: /f/ /l/ /a/ /g/ is flag (near-miss: bag; same rime, different onset)
/b/ /r/ /i/ /dj/ is bridge (near-miss: fridge; one sound differs)
pages_detail.title: Blend the Sounds

pages_detail.activities: Adult says the word once; the child says the first, middle, and last sounds; the adult writes what the child says in the three 40pt boxes. The boxes hold three selected sounds only, not every sound in the word.
pages_detail.title: Find the Sounds: Beginning, Vowel, Ending.

pages_detail.activities: Dots only. Adult says the word once; the child says each sound slowly, in order, and draws one dot in each sound box. The adult does not write phonemes in these boxes.
pages_detail.title: Say Every Sound
